synthetic_scenarios: In-memory fixture migrations only; not application release migrations.

checks.name: a previous synthetic schema has one committed migration journal row
upgrade from the first real migration preserves both tenants data
an already-applied exact manifest is a no-op
changed applied migration bytes are refused without database writes
missing or renamed applied versions are refused as divergent history
API actors cannot inspect or mutate the private migration journal
failure commits only earlier files and stops before later files
failed migration rolls back DML, RLS, policy, grants and function replacement
an unpublished unapplied fixture can be corrected and retried from its exact committed prefix
the existing API projection still works across additive schema expansion
an appended forward correction repairs a committed behavior bug without rewriting history
dry run inventories pending DDL but rolls back data, privileges, schema and journal
a failing dry run leaves the committed schema and journal unchanged
migration and maintenance executors share the same exclusion lock
in-flight migration blocks another maintenance worker
terminated connection rolls back pending DDL and leaves no applied record
retry after connection loss applies only the uncommitted migration
restart preserves journal, data and idempotent migration replay
missing extension prerequisite fails atomically from an empty database
dry run from empty verifies all real migrations and leaves no schemas behind
empty-to-current application commits each real checksum exactly once
unrecognized existing migration namespace is preserved and refused
database without the explicit local fixture marker is refused before DDL

limits: Local PostgreSQL fixtures only; no hosted target, credentials or Supabase migration history changed.
Session termination tests transaction interruption, not power-loss or provider-outage recovery.
No automatic destructive down-migration or database restore is performed.
